question.text: The probability of India winning a test match against Australia is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> Assuming the matches to be independent events, the probability that in a <math><mn>7</mn></math> match series India’s second win occurs at <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math> test is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>256</mn><mi>P</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
2nd win in 4th test ⇒ In the first 3 matches
there must be exactly 1 win
so, required probability =3C114134214
P=27256
